prompt:
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: A displacement-time graph for an object moving along a straight line. The curve begins at (0, 0) with a steep positive gradient and gradually becomes less steep (flattens out) until it becomes horizontal at t = 5.0 s.]
Which statement describes the motion of the object between t = 0 and t = 5.0 s?
options: The object moves in the positive direction with increasing speed.
The object moves in the positive direction with decreasing speed.
The object moves in the negative direction with constant speed.
The object is stationary throughout the interval.

answer.explanation: Displacement is increasing in the positive direction (positive gradient), but the curve becomes progressively less steep, meaning the gradient (velocity) decreases to zero. Thus, the object moves in the positive direction with decreasing speed.

distractor_explanations: Increasing speed would produce a curve that becomes progressively steeper, not flatter.
Correct: positive gradient means positive direction, and decreasing steepness means decreasing speed.
Motion in the negative direction would have a negative gradient.
The object is only stationary at t = 5.0 s where the tangent is horizontal, not throughout the interval.
hints: Gradient equals velocity on a displacement-time graph.
What happens to the steepness of the tangent as time progresses?
solution: B. The positive slope shows motion in the positive direction. The flattening curve indicates decreasing speed (deceleration).
teacher_walkthrough: Observe the sign of the gradient: it is positive, so the object is moving forward.
Observe the trend in gradient: tangents drawn at later times are shallower, meaning instantaneous velocity decreases.
At t = 5.0 s, the gradient reaches zero (object comes to rest). Option 2 correctly describes this motion.
